_about: Regression evals for oak-curriculum-principles. 'trigger_evals' test that the skill description fires for the right queries and not for near-misses (judge sees the full installed skill list and routes each query). 'quality_evals' are graded with assertions, comparing a with-skill run against a no-skill baseline. Re-run when the skill or the base model changes. Results from the first pass: triggering 22/22; quality with-skill 12/12 vs baseline 9/12.

trigger_evals.query: I'm writing our KS3 geography curriculum from scratch and want it to follow solid curriculum-design principles. Where do I start?
Review this Year 4 history unit I've drafted and tell me where it's weak on curriculum quality.
We're rewriting our science scheme of work. What should I think about for sequencing and vocabulary across years?
Help me write a curriculum intent statement for our primary art curriculum.
Draft a knowledge organiser for a Norman Conquest unit that's genuinely knowledge-rich.
What does 'ambitious for all' mean in practice for a mixed-attainment Year 9 maths class? I don't want to dumb it down.
I want to quality-assure our MFL medium-term plan against good curriculum design. Is there a rubric?
Check whether my draft fractions sequence matches how Oak orders it across the years.
Rewrite this paragraph about our curriculum so it sounds like Oak.
What are Oak's brand colours and fonts for our booklet cover?
Give me a fun two-minute starter to settle my Year 8 class before a photosynthesis lesson.
What does the EEF evidence say about the impact of feedback on attainment?

quality_evals.prompt: I'm designing a new Year 8 history unit on the British Empire and decolonisation for my school. Draft a unit outline I can build from — the structure, what to include, and the thinking behind it.
assertions: specifies substantive knowledge AND vocabulary to teach (not just topic titles)
addresses sequencing / prior knowledge and/or threads
addresses diversity of interpretations/voices without tokenism
frames accessibility as same ambitious content + scaffolding (not differentiation-down)
includes flexibility/adaptation and mapping to the national curriculum
includes a rationale (why designed this way)

quality_evals.prompt: Review this draft Year 7 science lesson for curriculum quality and say how to improve it. DRAFT: Objective 'Understand particles and the three states of matter'. Input mentions diffusion, sublimation and intermolecular forces. Activity: lower-ability pupils colour/copy labels; higher-ability pupils write a paragraph. Assessment: 'Name the three states of matter'. Note: slots in wherever there's a free lesson; no prior unit assumed.
assertions: flags untaught vocabulary (diffusion/sublimation/intermolecular used but not taught)
flags differentiation-that-lowers-expectations and recommends same content + scaffolding
flags weak sequencing / 'no prior unit assumed'
uses structured judgement (Secure/Developing/Not-yet-evident), located evidence, priority actions, and names strengths
